status: Accepted release-one MXF scope on 23 October 2026; not implemented or cut over.
purpose: MXF supported layouts and header navigation requirements review after explicit damage-policy approval.

proposedBellaRules.family: Supported Avid-compatible OP-Atom, including third-party Avid files and verified qualifier variants 0/1/2/3. No generic OP1a expansion or unproven all-zero OP compatibility.
proposedBellaRules.headerAdmission: Closed and complete initial Header Partition at byte zero, validated under agreed damage/ownership rules. Status is not proof of sound bytes.
proposedBellaRules.navigation: Partition pack, recognized optional alignment Fill, Primer; checked HeaderByteCount enclosing region beginning at Primer key. Stop after that metadata region.
proposedBellaRules.storage: Bounded reads, checked file/enclosing extents, needed compact values/lookups; skip unneeded definitions/payloads safely. No fixed first-N-MiB cap or unchecked HeaderByteCount allocation; release temporary storage.
proposedBellaRules.compatibility: Preserve known version-1 byte layout and supported label/local-set/private forms. Actual minor1.2 must not be rejected by requiring1.3. Future incompatible major unsupported.
proposedBellaRules.unsupportedStates: Open or closed-incomplete initial header, run-in, absent/unsafe initial region and unsupported pattern contribute no MXF metadata in this first-release path. They are not all automatically damaged. Physical row and eligible independent PMR/MDB/filesystem facts remain.
proposedBellaRules.noAutomaticRecovery: No footer/RIP/later-copy search, EOF packet walk, essence/index decoding, repair or byte resynchronization merely for these columns.
proposedBellaRules.tradeoff: Does not recover metadata requiring later header copies or provisional recording state; deliberately narrower than broad OldScanner/toolkit structural navigation.
proposedBellaRules.separateDecisions: Source priority, extra header-opening reasons and MXF concurrency remain separate. No runtime implementation or app cutover.
proposedBellaRules.performance: Removes unconditional traversal beyond selected header in design; scan time/memory benefit remains unmeasured.

selectedFileSummary.limits: Selected observations only; no complete metadata reparse, essence read, RIP validation, whole-file certification or physical-disk/performance measurement.

publicPrimarySources.title: SMPTE ST377-1:2019

mediaComposer.scope: Read-only, bounded installed Media Composer arm64 native ordinary MXF scan/import navigation and selected linked storage implementations. No application, private API, media parser execution, media mutation, build or test run.

findings.topic: Ordinary Avid MediaFiles scan operational-pattern gate
findings.meaning: The LocalMDB and MSMDB ordinary MXF scan functions create a MXFDomain, then admit OP-Atom or an all-zero operational pattern. Other patterns raise a native initialization error or return false. This does not establish that Media Composer cannot import OP1a through another route.
anchors: LocalMDBScanMXF.txt: MXFDomain::New call 0x41ba48, IsOPAtom call 0x41ba6c, IsNullOperationalPattern 0x41ba94, other-pattern error 0x41ba9c..0x41babc.
MSMDBScanMXF.txt: MXFDomain::New 0x44e3d4, IsOPAtom 0x44e3f8, nullOP 0x44e420, unsupported cleanup/false 0x44e650..0x44e674.

Fresh IsOPAtom 0x47b2a8 zeroes byte at sp+0xd before comparing the two 64-bit halves; do not describe it as a completely unmasked 16-byte equality. Fresh IsNullOperationalPattern 0x47b2e4 requires both halves zero.

findings.topic: Ordinary reader uses AAF-MXF storage, not the standalone older chunk helper
findings.status: verified static ordinary-call-route; concrete-storage selection not traced end to end
findings.meaning: MXFDomain initialization uses cached raw storage and creates/opens an AAF file over it. Installed libcom-api.dylib contains distinct generic, Avid, and OP1a storage implementations. A general toolkit behavior is not automatically the rule of the ordinary managed-media scan.
anchors: MXFDomainInit.txt: Create allocator 0x470924, AAFCreateRawStorageCached2 0x47097c, AAFCreateAAFFileOnRawStorage 0x4709f8, reading-open interface call 0x470a64, getHeader 0x470ee8.

KLVFactoryOpenRead 0x1b79ec creates OMMXFStorage at 0x1b7a0c. AvidFactoryOpenRead 0x197f10 reads the operational pattern, selects OMMXFOP1aStorage at 0x197fa8 for its matched OP1a label, otherwise OMAvidMXFStorage at 0x197f7c.

Factory vtable +0xc0 resolves to readOperationalPattern 0x1b7c1c. That function finds initial header, validates full key as header, reads BER length, skips 0x40 fixed partition-value bytes and reads the operational pattern at 0x1b7c8c..0x1b7c9c.

findings.topic: Initial header and run-in search exists in the installed toolkit
findings.meaning: The shared finder seeks to file start and searches in 100-byte blocks for a 14-byte header-key prefix. The outer loop has a 16-bit candidate-position guard checked between blocks; describe it as a bounded roughly 64 KiB search, not an exact maximum run-in promise. Later callers read the full key and test isHeader. This does not prove every Media Composer entry route accepts every run-in form.
anchors: FindHeader 0x1c457c: seek0 at 0x1c45ac..0x1c45b8, 100-byte read at 0x1c45e4..0x1c45fc, prefix match state 0x1c462c..0x1c4644, candidate>>16 guard 0x1c4658..0x1c4664.
Raw constant at VA 0x2a7bf0 is captured in raw-vtables.json; first14 bytes are 060e2b34020501010d0102010102.
IsHeader 0x1c4808 accepts all four initial header status keys (open/closed, complete/incomplete). The key recognizer itself is not a closed/complete-only gate.

findings.topic: Avid/generic metadata finder selects the initial header; toolkit also models HeaderByteCount
findings.status: verified toolkit implementation; not universal native priority
findings.meaning: OMAvidMXFStorage::findMetadata and OMMXFStorage::findMetadata tail-call the shared initial-header finder. OMKLVStoredObject::restore calls virtual findMetadata (+0x138), seeks to the returned position, reads the key, reads the partition when recognized, then restores metadata until endsMetadata. The read PartitionPack overload stores the typed HeaderByteCount at object+0x38; this does not establish that ordinary Media Composer uses HeaderByteCount as its sole metadata-reading limit.
anchors: ToolkitRestore.txt: +0x138 call at 0x1b157c..0x1b1584, returned-position seek 0x1b158c..0x1b159c, isPartition 0x1b15b8, partition-reader +0x1f0 call 0x1b15c8..0x1b15cc, endsMetadata 0x1b1944.

AvidReadPartitionPack 0x19c5d8 reads ThisPartition(+0x20), PreviousPartition(+0x28), FooterPartition(+0x30), HeaderByteCount(+0x38), IndexByteCount(+0x40), subsequent fields in fixed typed sequence; +0x38 destination setup 0x19c67c, read call 0x19c690.

findings.topic: Separate OP1a metadata selector explicitly checks status and can prefer footer metadata
findings.status: verified toolkit OP1a capability, not ordinary OP-Atom scan rule
findings.meaning: OP1a findMetadata starts at initial header. If its HeaderByteCount is nonzero, it records that initial candidate. A closed and complete initial candidate returns directly. Otherwise it tries locating a footer; it switches to footer only when footer is closed, complete, and has nonzero HeaderByteCount. If an initial metadata candidate existed, failure to obtain a better footer can retain that candidate; the function is not a universal rejection of open/incomplete initial metadata.
anchors: OP1aFindMetadata 0x1ba64c: initial header search/read 0x1ba670..0x1ba69c. Pack+0x38 HeaderByteCount read at 0x1ba6a0, stores initial candidate at 0x1ba6ac; isClosed 0x1ba6b4, isIncomplete 0x1ba6c0, closed+complete branch directly to return at 0x1ba6cc.
Fallback footer calls 0x1ba6e4/0x1ba704; footer status checks 0x1ba73c/0x1ba748; footer HeaderByteCount 0x1ba750; replaces candidate 0x1ba758.
isClosed/isIncomplete recognize the four header statuses and their body/footer variants. They are meaningfully used in the OP1a selector above, not merely discovered as unused symbols.

findings.topic: Footer/RIP operations are real separate toolkit paths
findings.status: verified toolkit capability, ordinary metadata-selection priority not established
findings.meaning: OP1a findFooter can use a recorded footer pointer, otherwise a valid/readable random index, then a near-end-of-file finder. The Avid storage stream-restoration path also chooses between RIP-based and ordinary stream restoration. These are real paths; stream/index restoration is not proof that ordinary OP-Atom metadata is merged from later headers or searched across the whole file.
anchors: OP1aFindFooter 0x1ba780: recorded footer pointer nonzero 0x1ba79c..0x1ba7a8; valid/readable random-index path 0x1ba7c8..0x1ba84c; final near-end footer helper call 0x1ba870. This narrow audit did not disassemble that final near-end helper or claim its exact search range.

AvidRestoreStreams 0x1a03d0: virtual +0x448 findRandomIndex call 0x1a047c..0x1a048c; chooses virtual +0x4f8 or+0x500 at 0x1a0490..0x1a04b4. Raw vtable maps these to restoreStreams(offset) and restoreStreamsFromRandomIndex.
AvidFindRandomIndex 0x19aa60 reads last4bytes at fileSize-4, checks candidate index sizes (recorded size, then recorded size-4) and returns candidate offset.

AvidRestoreStreamsOffset 0x1a04cc follows recorded footer and previous partition references; explicit exceptions include Footer not found at 0x1a08e4 and Partition Pack specifies invalid previous partition at 0x1a08b4. This is stream restoration, not a demonstrated best metadata-header selection policy.

bellaImplicationInference: First-release OP-Atom/initial-header scope, accepting only readable qualified selected metadata and avoiding footer/RIP rescue, is a Bella engineering choice. It is not an exact clone of every installed Media Composer reader.

Do not equate incomplete partition status with broken byte framing. A closed-but-incomplete header can still have usable individually qualified values, whereas an open header can carry an earlier metadata copy. Neither native selector alone proves all values in a specimen are correct.

Using validated HeaderByteCount to bound Bella selected-header reading, with checked arithmetic/file bounds and no fixed metadata MB cutoff, can be justified by the format plus chosen Bella scope; this audit does not prove Media Composer uses that exact sole bound.

Keep physical media inventory and independent database facts when a layout/header is unsupported or unusable. The ordinary native import refusal does not imply Bella should delete the physical-file row.
limits: Static disassembly and raw vtable bytes only; no crafted-file, corpus decoder, GUI or performance experiment.

Full dynamic factory registration/selection from the specific MXFDomain reading-open through every concrete storage subtype was not reconstructed. Fresh factory and vtable links establish capability and exact implementation, not blanket invocation frequency.
OP1a import/linking through alternate Media Composer routes (for example plugins) was not audited. The verified ordinary MediaFiles scan gate is narrower than the toolkit feature set.
No universal exact rule proven for selecting/merging arbitrary repeated metadata headers, or for all footer/RIP corruption and fallback conditions.
The standalone older MXFDomain chunk parser exists but is not the demonstrated modern ordinary scan implementation; its caps/behavior were not adopted.

mdvx.method: Fresh full arm64 disassembly and installed SHA; raw-code/function hashes, Mach-O constants and branch/call inspection. Same binary and full dump as damage audit. 39 complete relevant functions extracted. No application/private API/fixture/media execution.
mdvx.mainFinding: MDVx ordinary MXF reading is an initial-header OP-Atom route: it expects a header partition at current stream position, reads the first declared header metadata region, extracts four ordinary row facts and releases parser structures. No ordinary footer/RIP fallback, repeated-header reconciliation or open/in-progress validity policy is established. Linked library helpers are not evidence of their use here.

findings.fact: Normal application scanning first admits managed Avid media trees/folders and physical .mxf filenames; it creates physical rows independently. ScanEngine delegates to ScanCoordinator, which can SKIP opening a media header when qualified databases supply current required metadata. Only an opened MXF invokes prepareMxf→MxfReader→projection. Standalone QBuffer/GuardedDevice tests bypass folder admission, database scheduling and UI publication.

PartitionPack OperationalPattern and registered Preface.OperationalPattern are retained. No OP-Atom-only allow/deny check was found in the current normal MXF reader/preparation/projection route. The decoder can therefore accept more structural inputs than Bella's agreed Avid-compatible OP-Atom product scope. This is NOT evidence of complete OP1a/other workflow support.

partitionKey accepts key kind byte2/3/4 and status byte1–4, plus Body(kind3) status0x11. The reader does not select metadata differently for the four ordinary status values; it records kind/status. It does not establish a preferred closed/complete header or wait/retry an in-progress one. Status names/semantic guarantees require the separate format/native evidence.

Current Partition parser requires majorVersion==1 if at least two bytes are present, retains any minorVersion without a whitelist, and normalizes SMPTE registry-version byte7 for relevant key lookup. Those are separate version layers, not PMR record-set versions. Numeric minor2 in a major1 partition is not major2. The sole authored major-version rejection case changes major to2.

findHeader searches byte-by-byte for a recognized Header Partition key at offsets0 through maximumRunIn65535. Pointers/ThisPartition are interpreted relative to that found key. This is the source's run-in boundary, not a 64-KiB/64-MiB limit on metadata or file size. No dedicated run-in boundary test was found in the inspected current MXF test files.

Each partition starts fresh HeaderByteCount/Primer state. A header begins at the first non-Fill packet after the Partition Pack; one leading Fill is tolerated, more qualifies Malformed. Nonzero HeaderByteCount sets the end, checked against offset overflow and each packet's enclosing extent. A Header Partition with zero header bytes qualifies Malformed; Body/Footer can have zero. A following partition/EOF before declared region end qualifies the source.

Primer mappings are partition-local. Known local-set coding is 0x53(two-byte tags/two-byte lengths) or0x13(two-byte tags/BER lengths); exact Avid private-root UUID is specially handled with0x53. Unsupported local coding stays range-only. Relocated tags, missing/ambiguous mappings and duplicate Primers are qualified explicitly; no global familiar-tag fallback.

When opened, current reader walks every top-level KLV framing to EOF and parses metadata in encountered declared regions. It seeks over recording/index payloads and padding instead of reading essence. This is not a whole-file byte read; cost depends on packet/metadata structure. It has no normal early return after a usable initial header.

Footer/header copies encountered by the sequential KLV walk are retained separately. RIP entries/total length are parsed when encountered, but RIP is not used as a navigation seek table. Previous/footer pointers are checked AGAINST physically encountered partitions after the walk; they are not followed to discover them. No binary byte resynchronization after framing failure or automatic repair is implemented here. RIP entry targets are not all validated by checkPointers(), which only iterates Partition previous/footer pointer records.

Objects/references have partition context, independent roots and source-local master ownership. No first/last header wins in the reader. Higher layers can reconcile equal-priority observations from multiple copies; conflicting values can remain unresolved. This is broader than choosing one ordinary initial header and must not be described as the same policy.

Current reader retains earlier objects when a later KLV/physical payload is incomplete, interprets them and allows noncancelled preparation to project them. Whole-source Incomplete can describe a sound initial metadata region and a later truncated recording/footer, but the prior approved damage policy forbids publishing an unsafe selected-header prefix. A readable selected header does not certify playable media.

Physical extents and qint64 arithmetic are checked, reads use16-KiB chunks and opaque unsupported ranges are skipped. There is no arbitrary fixed-prefix/header-size cap. Full recognized Partition/Primer/RIP/Avid-directory values and local property data can still be retained before some validation; broad decoded graphs add storage. No per-job aggregate metadata/graph budget is established in this reader.
findings.qualification: Physical-file bounds do not by themselves guarantee small memory use. No memory/time measurement or exhaustion experiment was run.

findings.fact: Current test sources contain no metadata_beyond_64m_is_parsed symbol or tst_mxfparser.cpp file. Named legacy large-header test cannot be treated as a current passing test. Current5-GiB opaque-header test has needed metadata BEFORE the opaque payload, inside initial HeaderByteCount. Repeated-header test deliberately includes FOOTER metadata. These cases justify no arbitrary cap and explicit copy scope; they do not prove universal initial-header sufficiency.
findings.targetedSearch: Current tests/**/*.cpp and **/*.h for metadata_beyond/beyond.*64/late metadata/header64/run-in; no test execution or historical comparison performed.

recommendations.recommendation: Keep the agreed Avid-compatible OP-Atom scope, including needed Avid compatibility/private forms and the already agreed field rules. Do not widen to a general MXF/AAF loader simply because current generic framing accepts other OP labels.

For release-one ordinary closed/complete initial metadata, parse one fully validated initial HeaderByteCount region, its Primer and necessary ownership/context, then stop. This is a scoped proposed reading policy rather than proof that a later contradictory copy cannot exist. Native/actual-layout evidence must settle exact compatibility flags and the release-one version baseline.

Do not reintroduce a fixed64-KiB/64-MiB prefix cap. Needed metadata late WITHIN a trusted initial region remains eligible. Stream/seek across safely bounded unneeded values instead of buffering the whole declared region or whole file. Count/extent/resource checks precede allocation where possible; resource failure is not corruption.

Keep per-region Primer and only the necessary definitions/private wrappers proved required by retained fields. Preserve0x53/0x13 and observed Avid forms when qualified. Skip safely bounded unneeded definitions/opaque payloads early; do not discard every dictionary/private item indiscriminately.

Do not add a general EOF walk, every-header reconciliation, footer/RIP hunt, byte resynchronization or essence/index decoding by default. If initial metadata is missing/open/incomplete/unsupported, keep the physical row and availability outcomes; exact optional alternate-header recovery must be justified by native/actual evidence and separately agreed.

Apply the approved chosen-header structural/owner/field damage boundaries. A later body/footer error cannot automatically erase an independently trusted selected header, and an incomplete selected-header prefix cannot be promoted. Release temporary buffers/lookup graphs after compact extraction.
Do not interpret the four-PMR/four-MDB limits as media-header concurrency policy. Keep already agreed source-specific opening rules; broader priorities, extra opens and scheduling stay at the end.
